tests.name: the allowed-tool execution proof: a confirmed completed-call effect row for insrc_analyze and insrc_analyze_step under --enabled-tools connector_insrc_insrc_analyze/connector_insrc_insrc_analyze_step, tolerating connector flakiness via bounded retry -- an unresolved result here is accepted as 'stays unavailable', per review r3 finding 4, not a test failure

reported.evidence: Live run against the installed vibe 3.1.4 binary via qualifyReadOnlyCapability(context, {command:'vibe'}, 2): resolved status:'unavailable', reason 'allow-side probe: insrc_analyze and/or insrc_analyze_step did not show a confirmed completed call (attempt 2/2)' after 112.7s. Separately confirmed by direct interactive probing this session: the model's own live diagnostic reports the insrc MCP connector is not registered in its callable toolset in this environment, even though config.enabled_tools correctly lists the two connector_insrc_* tools as requested. This is the explicit accepted 'stays unavailable' outcome, not a defect in the suite -- it correctly detected genuine non-availability.

tests.name: the blocked-tool proof via structural catalog enumeration (no actual write attempted)

reported.evidence: Same live run's export.json config.enabled_tools contained exactly the two requested connector_insrc_* tools and nothing else -- every other (disallowed, including write/bash) tool was absent, proving the block structurally. No write tool call was ever attempted.

tests.name: the blanket-bypass absence proof via catalog enumeration

reported.evidence: Same live run: enabledToolsFrom(exportObj) contained no tool outside the two-tool allowlist, so the suite's bypass check (filter for tools not in `required`) found nothing and did not fire the bypass-absence failure path.

tests.name: the ac4 no-mutation proof via structural catalog evidence that write/bash tools are absent or denied, never via an actual write under the production profile

reported.evidence: Same live run's export.json confirms write_file/edit/bash-style tools are absent from config.enabled_tools under the pinned read-only descriptor; the qualification suite never attempts a real write -- the proof is structural-only, per the LLD's own design.

tests.name: the export.json effective-config fingerprint actually present and parsable on a real run

reported.evidence: Direct verification against a real captured export.json from an earlier live probe this session (vibe_version 3.1.4, 116 config keys): effectiveConfigFingerprintFrom's own logic (JSON.stringify({vibeVersion, config}) then sha256) produced a real, non-trivial 64-char hex fingerprint. The qualify run above did not reach this step itself since the allow-side check failed first, but the fingerprint-extraction logic itself is independently proven against real export.json content.
